Through federal preemption, EPA helps keep billions of Americans safe by setting standards and creating uniform labels and packaging for pesticides. Learn more by visiting croplifeamerica.org slash Federal Pesticide Regulation. This is Acropulse Open Mic. In her time in Washington, Vicki Hartzler has served on the Armed Services and the Agriculture Committees. Looking back, she's proud of accomplishments for her district while in office.

speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: Well, we did help right and pass two farm bills, and of course they're called farm bills, but really 80% of that actually doesn't go to farms because the food supplement programs like, now I call it SNAP, but these call it food stamps, women infants and children, school lunch programs, things. So that's really the bulk of it. But those programs are very, very important for rural Missouri and for the nation. If you look at the nutrition title, obviously, they have the support for people that are struggling. And children who are hungry need some food at school. But for agriculture, It's really important to have those safety net programs for when years. We have, you know, bad years and crops and prices so that we can keep afloat and keep going. And America will never be dependent on another country for our food supply. That puts us in a very, very risky place. And I say food security is national security. And I'm on Armed Services Committee too, but I go hand in hand. A hungry people are people who are dependent on other countries for their food are very, very vulnerable. We never want to be in that spot. So that's why we have the safety net programs. But the farm bill covers more than just the safety of programs. Obviously, crop insurance is critical partnership between the private industry as well as the government helping supplement that. But they have programs for rural America, including rural broadband. And I've been very proud to help past three amendments in the last farm bill to increase availability and the speed of rule broadband. You know, when I first took office, I would say almost three quarters of my district didn't have high speed internet. It was just very damaging and limiting the potential of school children couldn't access their homework, senior citizens, especially during COVID couldn't access telemedicine. Many of our small communities that are struggling have businesses who want to locate there, but without high-speed Internet, they were rejected. And so I've focused on trying to get that, and I'm so excited that two of my real electric co-ops cover 14 of my counties have now committed to and are putting fiber to every household and utilizing some of these grants and programs that we have passed in Congress. But there's other programs, rural community facility programs, I had an amendment passed in the Farm Bill that allowed more communities to be able to access that, to build more libraries and fire stations and those type of things. It's senior citizen housing that's in almost every one of our small towns. Those four plexes, that is USDA grants. USDA grants for sewer and water systems in our small towns and so many of our communities are having to replace those because they were first put in in the 50s and 60s. And so the Farm Bill encompasses So many things, and I was able, not only, we passed the conservation title, but it had an amendment in that Farm Bill to allow mid-term and mid-contract grazing for our cattlemen, for our CRP land. So we've done a lot of things in that Farm Bill and increased the amount of rule broadband, and those are some things I'm very proud of, and thankful I've had the opportunity to work on, as far as, well, You know, things I wish we could have gotten done. I've been working on a bill to try to help our cattle industry. They've really struggled the last few years. We've tried to get more transparency to them in the house. We passed part of my legislation to set up a USDA contract library where the meat packers would have to disclose the type of contracts that they are offering to different cattlemen. We have more leverage. You know what's going on. My bill also would require the Packers to report for the next 14 days to kill rates. So they know if there's going to be a day where they're going to be short cattle. And maybe that would provide some leverage for somebody. If they've got a potload of cattle that they could bring in that day and maybe negotiate a better price. And then set up a regional pricing on a cash basis to have a minimum level of that to get some more some more price discovery in the market. We haven't been successful in getting all of that done yet. But I'm glad to see the cattle market is starting to come back now on its own. So hopefully that will fix itself. But I still think more transparency is needed and more meatpacking plants. And I've been very supportive of and promoting trying to get more regional meatpacking plants. or cattleman have more options of where to take their cattle.
